chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah from someone else from Aban ibn Uthman from Muhammad al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic is, says in His Book: 'And purify My House for those who circumambulate it and stand to Pray and bow down and prostrate themselves.'
Thus, it is befitting for the servant that he does not enter Makkah except when he is clean, having washed his sweat and impurities, and purified himself.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on entering Makkah regarding ritual purity?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the pre-condition of physical purity (taharah) for entering Makkah, derived directly from the divine command in Surah Al-Hajj to purify the House for those who perform Tawaf, Qiyam, Ruku, and Sujud. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the sanctity of the city extending beyond ritual state to include the removal of bodily impurities like sweat and dirt, ensuring the pilgrim enters in a state of comprehensive cleanliness.

en.hubeali:
Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Sama’at, from someone else, from Aban Bin usman, from Muhammad Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic is Saying in Hisazwj Book [22:26] and purify My House for those who circumambulate it and stand to Pray and bow down and prostrate themselves.
Thus, it is befitting for the servant that he does not enter Makkah except when he is clean, having had washed his sweat, and body parts, and purified’.
en.sarwar: 3. Humayd ibn Ziyad has narrated from ibn Sama‘ah from more than one person from Aban ibn ‘Uthman from Muhammad al-Halabiy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Glorious, has said in His book, ‘Cleanse My house for those who perform Tawaf, and Ttikaf, those who do Ruku‘ and those who do Sajdah therein.’ [22:28]
A servant (of Allah) should not enter Makkah without cleansing, washing his perspiration and so on and without purification.’”
